messages.author: 6575e6b2b7f0ee01
messages.subject: לופ על משתנים בתוך DATAFRAME
parts:
Hi all

In this study I am looking for “good” transformation to describe change in 50 bacteria counts(cfu/gr) form  from visit 2 to visit 3 (after the merge- it is .x and .y).

Bacteria counts are “crazy” distributed and I have used the(log10+1) to stabilize variability in the per visits analysis.

 

My questions

1)      Is there elegant way to change the .x to .2  and .y to .3  after merge?

2)      Is there an elegant way to write a function  and run it in a loop on all the bacteria-variables?

So I can play with the transformation as I like?

 

This is the code I am using now, but it is not elegant (P.S. +1  to avoid the deviation in 0)

 

#Option1

datABF$Aerobic.cfu       <- datABF$Aerobic.cfu.y/  (datABF$Aerobic.cfu.x+1)

datABF$Coliforms.cfu     <- datABF$Coliforms.cfu.y/ (datABF$Coliforms.cfu.x+1)

datABF$Lactobacillus.cfu <- datABF$Lactobacillus.cfu.y/(datABF$Lactobacillus.cfu.x+1)

.

.

.

 

datABF$Clostridium.cfu   <- datABF$Clostridium.cfu.y/(datABF$Clostridium.cfu.x+1)

datABF$Pseudo.cfu        <- datABF$Pseudo.cfu.y/(datABF$Pseudo.cfu.x+1)

 

Diklah

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] לופ על משתנים בתוך DATAFRAME
parts:
Oops
I clearly misunderstood the problem.
This is more appropriate:

# Generate self contained example:

A <- matrix(runif(n*m), ncol = m, nrow=n) %>% as.data.frame
names(A) <- paste(LETTERS[1:10],rep(c('.x','.y'), each= 10), sep='')

# Start analysis:
the.names <- names(A) %>% gsub(pattern =".[xy]", replacement = '', x = .) %>% unique
for(.name in the.names){
  y <- A[paste(.name,'.y', sep='')]
  x <- A[paste(.name,'.x', sep='')]
  A[,.name] <- (y/log10(x+1))
}

I will also note that since you have this structure in the data, you might avoid the string handling tricks by saving the data in a list of matrices in stead of a flat single matrix. 

Hope this helps.
